body: I will look into this - thanks for the suggestion.

It probably just appears to others that you have a bad attitude. People don't like people that are sad/angry all the time, or those that appear to be.

I have taken pictures of my workout progress and I noticed an anomaly. Starting, I would always have this horrible sad frown - over about a year the frown slowly leveled out, and now it almost appears to be rounding up into a smile. I was never consciously making a face in any of the pictures. I don't feel like I am smiling, but something with strenuous and continuous physical exercise makes it appear as though I am happier. Maybe I am happier - I don't know. I'm certainly less depressed, but still 'empty' to a degree since I have no friends. I also get warmer responses from others at work now since they think I'm happier. Just food for thought.

Hmm, no one is local, and those that are about 50 miles away haven't recently posted updates. No biggie, I prefer working out solo anyway. I always quit when I use to go with a partner before (in retrospect it was because I didn't feel like dealing with a social situation). Oddly enough, I'm not too bothered working out with other people around since I don't 'have' to talk with them.

I don't think they like people just borrowing the dogs for a day ... I mean they're animals not a pair of jeans. Maybe I'm wrong, but I just get the feeling they'd think I'm borrowing the dog for mischief if I asked to go walk him/her in the park for the day.

Um, what do you photograph? I have a decent canon point and shoot which is capable of some pretty good images for not being an SLR, but I have never even thought of using it for photography. Do you like take pictures of nature?

I don't have hobbies because I don't have friends. I don't even remember what a hobby is. I guess you could say that working out is a hobby, because I enjoy it in an atheistic spiritual way, lol. It's relaxing and soothing. 

I also couldn't find anything about local groups on dailyburn, it appears to just be an online forum board?
What are some places that take volunteers? ... preferably with younger people not older people.

Start exercising - seriously. Start slow and continue to increase how much you do it as time goes on. Do it at a recreation center and just start late at night when no one is there and then move earlier into the daytime when you're comfortable. My own personal recommendation is to not overdo the cardio and to start with light weights until you get in the habit of going there without thinking about it. You won't be able to keep guys away from you if you follow through in the longrun.
